verdicts.strongest_argument: The whole observation lives in quote.json, which is the anchor both sides already hold: the sealed baseline reports avg_volume_20d of 254,685, spot 1.02, run_up_5d_pct 2.72% and realised_vol_20d of 13.2%, so the 1,676,400-share session and the break back above $1.00 are computable from the shared file without research. That does not make the flow uninformative, but it does mean nothing was uncovered. The interpretation is then self-cancelling in the finding's own words - 'either an accumulator or the company's own bid defending the NYSE $1 threshold' - and those two readings have opposite implications for the print: an accumulator front-running results is information, a listing-compliance bid is mechanical and says nothing about the numbers, and a third reading the finding does not consider, a single index or ADS-conversion block on a $1 name that had just traded a two-cent band for seven sessions, is at least as likely as either. A one-directional claim cannot be built on a mechanism that has not been identified. On magnitude, the finding is measured against an anchor I am told not to trust and which visibly cannot be trusted: baselines/WDH.json lists 2025-12-03 twice as two separate events, tags three of eight rows with session conflicts, is built on the weaker 6-K exhibit-text path, and - per the sealed brief - counts 2026-06-17 and 2026-06-23 as two prints when the Q1 release actually hit the tape on 2026-06-16 with no 6-K that day, while treating a 2026-07-24 16:01 ET 6-K as a print 46 days out. So expected_move_pct of 1.73% is not a usable band in either direction, and a claim whose size only looks material against that anchor is unmeasured rather than small. What I concede: the corpus publishes nothing about the 09-04 session, the news channel returned zero items across all ten sweeps, and one session of 6.6x volume on the eve of a bmo print is the kind of flow that is sometimes informed.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The entire captured commentary for the window is three posts; the 09-04 one reads the chart as 'quite board' and needing 1.30 to break the downtrend, i.e. nobody attached a cause to the volume - this is the corpus being silent, not publishing.
No filing of any kind between the 2026-07-24 6-K and the print, so there is no disclosed corporate action - including no announced buyback tranche - to which the 09-04 volume can be attributed.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json, bmo name so 2026-09-04 is the last admissible bar: closes of 0.994, 0.995, 0.995, 0.993, 0.985, 0.976, 0.973 from 08-25 to 09-02 on 138,800-208,300 shares, then 1.02 on 1,676,400 - 6.6x the 254,685 average and 8.3x the prior session. That is a genuine break of a seven-session two-cent pin. Against it: the baseline's reaction history is mis-specified (duplicate 2025-12-03 rows, three session conflicts, 6-K text-matched rather than item-coded, and the brief establishes the Q1 print date is wrong), so I have no defensible statement of how much a WDH print normally moves and I am not treating the 1.73% median as one.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Any dated attribution for the 09-04 block - a 13G/13D, an announced repurchase tranche, or an index-rebalance notice - would resolve the ambiguity; identifying it as informed accumulation rather than a compliance or mechanical bid would push this well below 40.

interactions: none - single claim. Its one corroborating datapoint, the 'GSE market share increased to 15%' post of 2026-09-03, comes from the same three-message digest and the hunter states it could not be traced to a company release, so it is untraceable rather than independent.
corpus_limits: This capture is an EDGAR index plus a three-message Stocktwits dump; the news channel returned zero items across all ten sweeps, so there is no wire copy, no preview, no consensus and no explanation for the 09-04 session available to me at all. That silence is a capture artefact of the queries run and I have scored it as uncertainty, not as evidence of non-publication. The 6-K bodies are not stored, so I could not check whether any of the matched filings is actually a results release. WDH's session is inferred from 6-K exhibit text rather than measured, the reaction history double-counts 2025-12-03 and, per the sealed brief, measures the wrong day for Q1 2026 and probably counts a non-print on 2026-07-24 - so expected_move_pct is built on a broken event list. No option chain. No tripwire-flagged documents excluded.
